name: Walter of Chatillon (Gualterus de Castellione)
bio: Walter of Chatillon (Gautier de Chatillon, Gualterus de Castellione) was a French poet and cleric of the twelfth century, born about 1135 in the north of France. He studied at Paris, and is named as a pupil of Stephen of Beauvais. He wrote Latin verse of several kinds, among them rhymed satires and love and spring songs in the manner of the wandering scholars, some of which were copied into the Carmina Burana.

His fame in his own century rested on the Alexandreis, an epic of ten books in about 5,400 hexameters on the career of Alexander the Great, drawn chiefly from the Roman historian Quintus Curtius Rufus and dedicated to William of the White Hands, archbishop of Reims. It was read and imitated in schools for generations after, and one of its lines, 'Incidis in Scyllam cupiens vitare Charybdim', passed into proverb.
